news.headline: Invivyd Announces Positive Topline Results from LIBERTY Phase 3 Study Demonstrating VYD2311 Safety and Tolerability Superior to mRNA-based COVID-19 Vaccine; Announces Regulatory Submission Plans for VYD2311
news.body: VYD2311 met all primary and secondary endpoints comparing VYD2311 to an mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine, demonstrating VYD2311 safety and tolerability that is clinically and statistically superior to the safety and tolerability of an mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccineVYD2311 combined with an mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine demonstrated no interference with vaccine-induced neutralizing titers, and instead added substantially to vaccine-induced neutralizing titersVYD2311 observed profile in LIBERTY indicates high measured neutralizing antiviral titers supporting the target profile for VYD2311 under study in the DECLARATION pivotal clinical studyInvivyd plans for DECLARATION and LIBERTY clinical studies to be the basis of a planned Biologics License Application (BLA) submission for VYD2311 to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration via Accelerated Approval Program following a recent Type C meeting; DECLARATION topline data on safety and immunogenicity to support the submission are now expected in October; DECLARATION clinical efficacy data will be planned to be unblinded post-Accelerated Approval, if granted, subject to clinical event accrual Investor call to be held at 8:30 am ET on September 29, 2026 NEW HAVEN, Conn., Sept. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Invivyd, Inc. (Nasdaq: IVVD) today announced positive, clinically meaningful, and statistically significant topline data from the LIBERTY Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, active controlled study evaluating the safety and tolerability of (1) VYD2311, Invivyd’s investigational COVID-directed monoclonal antibody candidate, (2) mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine COMIRNATY® (mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine, COVID-19 mRNA vaccine, or COVID vaccine), and (3) VYD2311 co-administered with mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine. The study also evaluated the potential for immunologic interference between VYD2311 and mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine. LIBERTY is a companion study to DECLARATION, the ongoing placebo-controlled pivotal study of VYD2311 for pre-exposure prophylaxis of symptomatic COVID-19.

news.headline: Takeaways from AP investigation into collapse of housing towers during Venezuela's earthquakes
news.body: The collapse of public housing in Venezuela's La Guaira state after two June earthquakes is linked to decisions made in 2010. Experts say the government rushed to build apartments on unstable soil after mudslides displaced over 100,000 people. The buildings couldn't withstand the earthquakes, which scientists have now determined led to one of the largest ground motions ever documented in the world. The area’s proximity to a fault line and the height of the buildings increased risks. The government hasn't provided crucial data or blueprints and experts urge a careful rebuilding approach. They warn the cost of earthquake-resistant construction may deter future development. Over 6,500 people died in the June event.

logs.summary:
A powerful earthquake, initially measured at magnitude 7.1 (later revised to 6.8), struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan on July 28, 2026, at 4:27 p.m. local time. The quake caused the partial collapse of the Aeon Mall in Kashima, trapping many people and leaving an unknown number dead, while injuring at least 50 others and causing widespread damage including fires, power outages, and damage to historic Kumamoto Castle.
A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck southern Japan's Kyushu island near Kumamoto on July 28, 2026, causing a shopping mall to partially collapse with multiple people trapped and feared dead. The quake knocked out power to thousands of homes, ruptured roads, triggered a temporary tsunami advisory, and left dozens injured, with up to 30 mall employees missing after an explosion.

Rocky Mount, Virginia issued a voluntary water conservation request due to ongoing drought conditions, with the town receiving only about half its normal rainfall. Recent reports show drought persisting across several regions: central Minnesota's drought held steady while statewide conditions eased slightly, and eastern Idaho farmers are expecting lower potato yields due to drought and heat. Alabama's drought has been increasing, especially in southern and western areas, while St. Thomas has deteriorated into exceptional drought even as Puerto Rico saw slight improvement. Forecasts warn of a potentially unprecedented El Niño in 2026/27 that could bring below-normal rainfall to South Africa, and drought combined with the Black Sea grain crisis is raising global food security concerns, while El Niño-driven drought in Papua New Guinea has forced school sports cancellations.

logs.summary: Severe thunderstorms, tornadoes, and flash flooding impacted multiple regions across the United States from August 20–24, 2026. Confirmed tornadoes struck in Atlantic Beach (Long Island), Dover (Delaware), and York/Lancaster counties (Pennsylvania), while prolonged power outages from earlier storms left thousands without electricity in Gary, Indiana, for over a week. Widespread damage from downed trees, damaged homes, and flooding was reported in the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, Southeast, and Midwest.

No immediate reports of significant damage or casualties were noted in the selected news.
